topic: Pilates Is Booming. Chuze Fitness Is Taking a Different Approach.

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Pilates Is Booming. Chuze Fitness Is Taking a Different Approach.

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Reformer Pilates has become one of the fitness industry’s most in-demand workouts, but high prices, fixed class schedules and waitlists can make it difficult for members to participate. Chuze Fitness is working to remove those barriers by bringing Reformer Pilates into its larger club environment through a hybrid studio model. Launching in select locations, the Reformer Pilates studios are designed exclusively for MAX members, giving them access to: FreeMotion Reform RX-S Reformers in dedicated, purpose-built studio spaces. Hybrid Studio Model: Half the reformers support instructor-led group classes; the other half feature integrated video kiosks with guided, on-demand programming, so members can work out on their own schedule. 300-plus iFIT-powered classes across beginner, intermediate and advanced levels. No per-class fees; access is included for MAX members. Chuze’s CMO, Cheryl Barnett , said the company has been exploring Reformer Pilates for years. Although the brand recognized the opportunity, its research also revealed operational challenges, including instructor recruitment and training, as well as the potential for beginners to feel intimidated by the equipment and its spring adjustments. “Seeing the Freemotion RX reformer, with its enclosed springs and supporting training program, helped us see a path that fit Chuze,” explained Barnett.

topic: LeBron and Whoop Partner as Health Tracker Keeps IPO in Sight

facts.label: Story
facts.value: LeBron and Whoop Partner as Health Tracker Keeps IPO in Sight

facts.label: Article
facts.value: LeBron James was an early Whoop adopter, and the health tracker and NBA star have now formalized their relationship 11 years later via an endorsement. Health and fitness tracker Whoop has signed LeBron James as its newest global ambassador. It marks a full-circle moment for the brand and NBA star, who started wearing a Whoop in 2015 as one of its first 100 members, long before health wearables became ubiquitous. James will star in multimedia ad campaigns for Whoop, which currently has 3.5 million active paying members. “LeBron is one of the greatest examples of longevity in professional sports,” Whoop founder and CEO Will Ahmed said via email. “What’s exciting about this partnership is that we get to tell that story together and show people that performance isn’t just about what you do on the court. It’s about how you take care of yourself every day, over time.” James set a record last year by suiting up for his 23rd NBA season, topping Vince Carter’s longevity record. James extended the record this year when he signed a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers . The NBA’s all-time leading scorer, who turns 42 in December, isn’t just coasting as he approaches the finish line—he averaged nearly 21 points per game last year.

en.headline: LeBron and Whoop Partner as Health Tracker Keeps IPO in Sight
